title: Guardrails and data governance
summary: Keeps restricted data out of agents, repos and ineligible models: restricted paths and how they are enforced, which providers may receive internal and confidential data, prompt logging and which hosts may handle restricted data.

questions.prompt: Which paths hold restricted data (secrets, keys, credentials)? Detected sensitive paths are added to the standard patterns.

Which restricted path patterns get a mode other than deny? use:<pattern> lets a go-getter tool pass the content to a process without the agent reading it; sink:<pattern> lets a go-getter tool write it from a declared source without reading it back. Until go-getter secret run and put exist, both stay denied like deny.

options.label: Host hook blocks agent access and CI fails if one is tracked
options.tradeoff: Holds even when the agent ignores instructions; hosts differ in what their hook can see, so the coverage report shows the tier per host.

options.label: CI and pre-push fail if one is tracked
options.tradeoff: Stops leaks into git only; the agent can still read the files.

options.label: Instruction only
options.tradeoff: No friction; depends on the agent complying.

questions.prompt: Which models may receive internal data?

options.label: Approved cloud providers on paid, no-training terms
options.tradeoff: Keeps routing flexible across providers; requires paid API tiers and trust in provider terms.

options.label: One approved provider
options.tradeoff: One contract to audit; no cross-provider routing for internal data.

options.label: Local models only
options.tradeoff: Nothing leaves the machine; only some hosts can reach local models and quality is lower.

questions.prompt: Which provider is the approved one?
Does confidential data require a zero-data-retention endpoint?

options.label: No: confidential data goes where internal data may go
options.tradeoff: Works without a retention agreement; the class stays distinct for audit and path rules.

options.label: Yes: only zero-data-retention or local models
options.tradeoff: Strongest guarantee; confidential steps go to a human until a provider is recorded with zero data retention.

options.label: No confidential class
options.tradeoff: Fewer classes to maintain; confidential-looking data is handled as restricted.

questions.prompt: When is host prompt and content logging disabled?

options.label: On every host that has a setting for it
options.tradeoff: No prompt content in host telemetry, so no restricted content leaks into it; you lose prompt-level debugging.

options.label: Only on hosts permitted near restricted data
options.tradeoff: Keeps prompt logging on other hosts; relies on the hosts rule being right.

options.label: Leave host defaults
options.tradeoff: No changes; some hosts log prompts unless told not to.

questions.prompt: Which host agents may handle restricted data?

options.label: Hosts with a blocking pre-tool hook
options.tradeoff: Matches what the hook runtime can enforce; the coverage report flags hosts where DLP is only advisory.

options.label: All hosts
options.tradeoff: No restriction; hosts without enforcement rely on instructions.

options.label: Only hosts with an OS sandbox

decisions.title: Restricted data lives at a declared list of paths
decisions.body:
## Decision

The restricted data class is the paths {{answer.restricted-paths}} (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}). Agents do not read or write them, and only a local model may receive their content.

## Why

DLP needs a declared list that hooks and CI can enforce (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Restricted paths have an access mode, deny unless listed
decisions.body:
## Decision

A restricted path pattern listed in `go-getter.restricted-modes` as `use:<pattern>` or `sink:<pattern>` has that mode; every other one is `deny` (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}). Until `go-getter secret run` and `go-getter secret put` exist, `use` and `sink` paths are denied like `deny` paths, except to a call that is exactly `go-getter secret run` (for `use`) or `go-getter secret put` (for `sink`).

## Why

Agents need secrets they can use or fill without reading them, and no other go-getter command may be the exemption, since one that runs a user-supplied command would leak the content (decision 0072).

decisions.title: Restricted paths are blocked in the host and never committed
decisions.body:
## Decision

A host pre-tool hook blocks tool calls that touch a restricted path (tier 2) and CI and pre-push fail if one is tracked (tier 3) (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

DLP must not depend on agent compliance (decisions 0009, 0018).

guardrails.title: Agents must not touch restricted paths and none may be committed

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given restricted data must not reach a model or a repository (0018), the host must block access and git must refuse the files, since instructions alone fail silently.

enforcement.check: Pre-tool hook blocks tool calls that touch a restricted path
No tracked file matches a restricted path

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Never read, write or commit a path on the restricted list. The host hook blocks tool calls that mention one where the host supports it; git hooks and CI fail when a tracked file matches.

decisions.title: Restricted paths are never committed
decisions.body:
## Decision

CI and pre-push fail if a tracked file matches a restricted path (tier 3) (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A public history is world-readable (decision 0018).

guardrails.title: No restricted path may be committed

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given committed secrets are exposed to everyone with repository access (0018), git must refuse them.

enforcement.check: No tracked file matches a restricted path

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Never commit a path on the restricted list. Git hooks and CI fail when a tracked file matches.

decisions.title: Restricted paths are protected by instruction only
decisions.body:
## Decision

Agents are told not to read, write or commit restricted paths; nothing blocks them (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The project accepted the risk for less friction.

guardrails.title: Agents must not read, write or commit restricted paths

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the project chose no mechanical block, the rule rests on the agent following it.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Never read, write or commit a path on the restricted list. Advisory (tier 1): nothing blocks it.

decisions.title: Internal data goes only to approved cloud providers on paid no-training terms
decisions.body:
## Decision

Internal data may go to local models and to anthropic, openai and google on their paid API tiers. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

Providers count as approved only on their paid API tier; free tiers may train on content. Routing removes every model of another provider before it compares cost (guardrail routing-governance-before-cost). Add providers or local models by a new decision or a fact carrying `go-getter.models`.

## Why

Routing for cost must never move data outside the boundary its class allows (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Internal data goes only to {{answer.provider}} and local models
decisions.body:
## Decision

Internal data may go to local models and to {{answer.provider}} on its paid API tier. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

Providers count as approved only on their paid API tier; free tiers may train on content. Routing removes every model of another provider before it compares cost (guardrail routing-governance-before-cost). Add providers or local models by a new decision or a fact carrying `go-getter.models`.

## Why

Routing for cost must never move data outside the boundary its class allows (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Internal data stays on local models
decisions.body:
## Decision

Internal data may go to local models only. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

Providers count as approved only on their paid API tier; free tiers may train on content. Routing removes every model of another provider before it compares cost (guardrail routing-governance-before-cost). Add providers or local models by a new decision or a fact carrying `go-getter.models`.

## Why

Routing for cost must never move data outside the boundary its class allows (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Confidential data may go wherever internal data may
decisions.body:
## Decision

Confidential data goes to the models internal data may go to. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Confidential data needs a retention guarantee only some teams have contracted (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Confidential data requires zero data retention
decisions.body:
## Decision

Confidential data goes only to local models and to providers recorded with zero data retention. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Confidential data needs a retention guarantee only some teams have contracted (decision 0018).

decisions.title: There is no confidential data class
decisions.body:
## Decision

The project has no confidential class; confidential-looking data is handled as restricted. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Confidential data needs a retention guarantee only some teams have contracted (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Host prompt logging is disabled on every host
decisions.body:
## Decision

`go-getter apply` switches off prompt and content logging in every host setting that has one (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A host that logs prompts by default would copy restricted content into its telemetry (decision 0018).

guardrails.title: Host prompt logging must stay disabled

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given host telemetry can export prompt content, a restricted path read once would leave the machine through logs, so the setting must be off wherever the host exposes it.

enforcement.check: Host settings files that exist have prompt logging switched off

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Keep prompt and content logging disabled in host settings; `go-getter apply` sets it and the check fails when a settings file turns it back on.

decisions.title: Host prompt logging is disabled on hosts permitted near restricted data
decisions.body:
## Decision

`go-getter apply` switches off prompt and content logging on the hosts permitted near restricted data (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Prompts on those hosts may contain restricted content (decision 0018).

guardrails.title: Host prompt logging must stay disabled on hosts near restricted data

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given host telemetry can export prompt content, hosts that may handle restricted data must not log it.

enforcement.check: Settings files of hosts permitted near restricted data have prompt logging switched off

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Keep prompt and content logging disabled on hosts permitted near restricted data; `go-getter apply` sets it and the check fails when a settings file turns it back on.

decisions.title: Host prompt logging keeps host defaults
decisions.body:
## Decision

Host prompt and content logging settings are left as the hosts ship them (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The project accepted the leak risk of default prompt logging.

decisions.title: Restricted data is handled only on hosts with a blocking pre-tool hook
decisions.body:
## Decision

Only host agents with a blocking pre-tool hook handle restricted data; `go-getter coverage` shows each host's tier for guardrails and DLP (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Where a host cannot block, DLP is advisory (decision 0018).

guardrails.title: Restricted data is handled only on hosts with a blocking pre-tool hook

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given DLP must not depend on agent compliance (0018), only hosts whose hook can block may be near restricted data.

enforcement.check: Instruction; the coverage report shows the tier per host

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Handle restricted data only in host agents with a blocking pre-tool hook. Advisory (tier 1): `go-getter coverage` shows where DLP is only advisory.

decisions.title: Any host may handle restricted data
decisions.body:
## Decision

No host is excluded from restricted data; `go-getter coverage` shows each host's tier (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The project accepted advisory DLP on hosts that cannot block.

decisions.title: Restricted data is handled only on hosts with an OS sandbox
decisions.body:
## Decision

Only host agents with an OS sandbox handle restricted data (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A sandbox contains what a tool call can reach even when a hook misses it (decision 0018).

guardrails.title: Restricted data is handled only on hosts with an OS sandbox

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given a hook can miss a path, only hosts that also contain tool calls in an OS sandbox may be near restricted data.

enforcement.check: Instruction; the coverage report shows the tier per host

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Handle restricted data only in host agents with an OS sandbox. Advisory (tier 1).
